entities.summary:
Fra Giovanni da Fiesole, known posthumously as Fra Angelico, was an Italian Dominican friar and painter active during the early Florentine Renaissance.

Born in the late 13th century, Fra Angelico's early life is shrouded in mystery, but it is believed he was born in Fiesole, near Florence, Italy.

He began his artistic career in the 1340s, working under the tutelage of the renowned artist Giotto in the Scrovegni Chapel in Padua, Italy.

Fra Angelico's unique style, characterized by his use of gold leaf and intricate details, became renowned throughout Italy, and he was commissioned to create frescoes in the church of Santa Maria sopra Minerva in Rome.

During the 1450s, Fra Angelico traveled extensively throughout Italy, painting altarpieces for various churches and monasteries, including the Convent of San Marco in Florence.

Fra Angelico's most famous work, the 'Canticle of the Sun', is believed to have been painted in the 1420s.

He died on March 27, 1455, in Rome, Italy.

Fra Angelico's legacy extends far beyond his artistic contributions, as he played a significant role in the spiritual and cultural revival of the Renaissance.

In his later years, Fra Angelico became increasingly devoted to the Dominican Order, and his work reflects a deepening spirituality and mysticism.

Fra Angelico's life and art continue to inspire artists, scholars, and spiritual seekers to this day.

Fra Angelico's frescoes in the Scrovegni Chapel, for example, are considered some of the most beautiful and expressive works of the Early Renaissance.

The 'Canticle of the Sun', which Fra Angelico painted in the 1420s, is a masterpiece of Renaissance art, and its beauty and spirituality continue to captivate audiences around the world.

Fra Angelico's artistic legacy extends beyond Italy, as his work has influenced artists and artists across Europe.

Fra Angelico's frescoes in the Convent of San Marco in Florence are a testament to his enduring artistic genius.
